nodes.summary: ESP event-speaker PUT body contract is { speakerId, speakerType, ordinal, creationTime, modificationTime } and nothing else
nodes.details: Per ESP OpenAPI, /v1/events/:eventId/speakers/:speakerId PUT accepts only those five fields. Echoing the full GET response (spreading dependentData) fails server-side validation and has been the root cause of repeated 400s on edit. When using callWithDependency's body-builder, fall back to dependentData per-field: body.X ?? dependentData.X. creationTime and modificationTime are server-issued; do not let callers override them. The same pattern applies to all ESP PUTs on speaker resources.

nodes.summary: Session-time helpers must return SessionTimeInfo so React state can update without a page refresh
nodes.details: createSessionTimeForSession and upsertSessionTimeForSession previously returned Promise<void>, which dropped the API's sessionTimeId, creationTime, and modificationTime on the floor. Calling components could not update local state with the new optimistic-concurrency values, so users saw stale data and had to refresh the page after every session-time edit. Fix is to return the API response from both helpers and have handleAddSession / handleUpdateSession capture and propagate sessionTimeId + creationTime + modificationTime into local React session state. This is the EMC-wide convention for any API helper that yields server-issued timestamps.

nodes.summary: Spreading a GET response back into an ESP PUT body trips readOnly.openapi.validation
nodes.details: ESP marks several fields as read-only on PUT (e.g. targetCms on /v1/series/:id). Series unpublish / archive / external-update flows previously echoed the full GET response into the PUT body, which fails ESP's OpenAPI validator with readOnly.openapi.validation. Fix: always filter the payload through the resource-specific prepareEsp*PutPayload helper before PUT. For series use prepareEspSeriesPutPayload (wraps filterSeriesData in 'update' mode). For events use prepareEslEventPutPayload. New ESP PUT endpoints should add a sibling helper in utils/dataFilters.ts before the call site is added.

nodes.summary: ESP resources use modificationTime for optimistic concurrency on PUT; clients must round-trip it
nodes.details: Every ESP PUT on an updatable resource (event, series, session, speaker) requires the modificationTime field to match the server's last-known value. If they differ, PUT returns 409 with the current server state. Clients must therefore: (a) capture modificationTime on every GET, (b) send it back unchanged on the next PUT, (c) re-fetch on 409 and merge. Dropping or recomputing modificationTime client-side is the most common cause of silent edit failures on EMC.

nodes.summary: Per-resource PUT payload sanitizers live in utils/dataFilters.ts and follow prepareEsp{Resource}PutPayload naming
nodes.details: Convention adopted across the EMC frontend: every ESP PUT endpoint has a corresponding prepareEsp{Resource}PutPayload function in web-src/src/utils/dataFilters.ts that calls filterSeriesData (or the resource-specific equivalent) in 'update' mode. This centralizes read-only-field stripping and ensures unpublish, archive, and external-update flows all go through the same validation layer. Do not invent ad-hoc filtering at the call site.

nodes.summary: Claude agent access policy: read-only commands auto-approved, destructive operations require explicit approval; word-boundary matching prevents false positives in command filtering.
nodes.details: The EMC repo grants Claude agent file-edit permissions without prompting (defaultMode: acceptEdits) but enforces approval gates on destructive operations. Allowed commands (ls, cat, grep, find, echo, pwd, which) use word-boundary matching in Bash regex — e.g., Bash(ls *) matches 'ls -la' but not 'lsof', preventing accidental approval of unintended commands. Denied list includes rm -rf *, git push *, git reset --hard *, git merge *, and any --force flags. This pattern balances agent velocity (no friction on safe reads/edits) against repository safety (human-in-loop for irreversible changes).

nodes.summary: RSVP field metadata is loaded from external event-libs config via configService.getRsvpConfig; boolean attendee fields render as 'Yes'/'No' in UI and CSV exports.
nodes.details: RegistrationFieldsComponent loads RSVP field catalogs via configService.getRsvpConfig (with caching/retry), and renders each field's Label from the JSON config. In AttendeeTableComponent, boolean columns (e.g., requiresSxswTicket) display as 'yes'/'no' in table cells; AttendeeFiltersComponent maps filter chips to 'Yes'/'No'; ExportDialog normalizes boolean columns to 'Yes'/'No' in CSV. The field definition lives in external event-libs experiencecloud.json (not in EMC repo), following the Type/Options conventions of other Experience Cloud RSVP fields. Add requiresSxswTicket?: boolean to attendee.ts type definitions.

nodes.summary: Do not spread GET response objects directly into ESP series PUT bodies; omit read-only fields like targetCms using prepareEspSeriesPutPayload.
nodes.details: ESP enforces read-only constraints on series PUT endpoints (updateSeriesExternal, publishSeries, unpublishSeries, archiveSeries). The Series Dashboard receives full series objects from GET /series/{id}, which include targetCms. Callers must filter these via prepareEspSeriesPutPayload (in web-src/src/utils/dataFilters.ts) before PUT, which wraps filterSeriesData(..., 'update') to drop non-updatable fields. POST (createSeriesExternal) does not apply this filter—targetCms is allowed on create. This pattern prevents readOnly.openapi.validation errors and ensures consistency across all series mutation helpers.

nodes.summary: Page metadata (PPN) fields require explicit user acknowledgment before save; use sentinel id 'no-${fieldKey}' to distinguish explicit *No* selection from unset state.
nodes.details: EventFormData tracks metadataFieldAcknowledged (UI-only boolean map) to enforce that users must open each product/category dropdown and choose either a value or the *No* option before draft/publish. The *No* option uses stable id no-${fieldKey} (not startsWith('No ')) to persist correctly. After API load or successful save, hydrate acknowledgments so existing events remain usable without forced re-picking. Validate page-metadata fields only when catalogue fields exist. This prevents silent defaults and ensures intentional metadata decisions.

nodes.summary: Attendee table columns follow a fixed positional contract: Registered Date appears immediately before RSVP Status and Checked In, regardless of Campaign ID visibility.
nodes.details: The Registrations attendee table (AttendeeTableComponent.tsx, AttendeeFiltersComponent.tsx) maintains a strict column order where Registered Date is positioned before RSVP Status and Checked In columns. The column sources data from attendee.creationTime, formats it as MM/DD/YYYY for display, but uses numeric epoch values for sorting to ensure correct chronological order. Export dialogs (ExportDialog.tsx) must include Registered Date in the default column set. This ordering invariant applies across all visibility states, including when Campaign ID is conditionally shown.

nodes.summary: Unified search across resource metadata and nested relations (group + members) requires debounced query coordination, parallel prefetch, and match-type badges to disambiguate result sources.
nodes.details: When implementing search that spans a parent resource (group) and its nested relations (members), use `onDebouncedQueryChange` and `searchLoading` props on the dashboard layout to coordinate async prefetch of related data (e.g., `getGroupUsers` calls) in parallel with the main query. Render match-type badges (e.g., 'Group match' vs 'Member match') to clarify which field matched. Auto-expand rows with member matches and scope the expanded panel's member list by the active query to avoid showing unrelated members. This pattern lives in `ResourceDashboardLayout` (coordination layer) and `ScopeGroupManagement` (search filter + prefetch logic).

nodes.summary: Event Title and EN Title fields have a 150-character max length constraint; this is a UI-enforced limit that likely mirrors a backend validation rule.
nodes.details: The EventInfoComponent.tsx form enforces a 150-character maximum on both the localized Event Title field and the English title for page URL field. This constraint should be treated as a durable API contract—any backend validation (in events-service-platform or events-service-layer) likely enforces the same 150-char boundary. When building PUT/POST payloads for event creation/update, truncate or validate titles to ≤150 chars before submission to avoid silent failures or backend rejection.

nodes.summary: Speakers and sponsors are grouped by role/tier with per-group drag-and-drop reordering; role/tier changes move items to the end of the new group and trigger per-group ordinal recomputation.
nodes.details: In SpeakersComponent.tsx and SponsorsComponent.tsx, items are grouped by speakerType and tier respectively. Drag-and-drop is restricted to within-group moves only (cross-group drops are blocked). When a speaker's role or sponsor's tier is changed via inline picker, the item is moved to the end of the new group. On save, onAfterSave computes per-group ordinals for both components. SponsorData now includes an optional ordinal field, and updateSponsorInEvent in api.ts explicitly preserves ordinal in the merge logic. Both components display a disclaimer note that group display order on the DA page is governed by template configuration, not EMC form ordering.

nodes.summary: RSVP field option panels render inline within the field card with conditional icon toggle; drag interactions collapse all open panels to enforce mutual exclusivity.
nodes.details: In RegistrationFieldsComponent.tsx, option panels for RSVP fields (select, multi-select) now render as children inside the field card border rather than as sibling elements below. The expand/collapse trigger is a ListBulleted icon in a 5th grid column (only rendered for fields with selectable options via rsvpFieldDefinitions.ts). The icon highlights in selection-ring color when open. Starting a field drag operation collapses all open option panels—this is a deliberate UX constraint to prevent simultaneous drag and panel interactions. Option rows no longer have individual borders; drag-over ring feedback is retained. Fields without options have no list icon and no extra column gap.

nodes.summary: Event speaker PUT request body must be contract-shaped; do not spread raw GET response into PUT payload.
nodes.details: The API service layer enforces a specific payload shape for speaker PUT operations (web-src/src/services/api.ts). When updating event speakers, construct the request body to match the server's expected contract rather than spreading the GET response directly. This prevents field mismatches and validation failures. See Sessions and EventForm components for correct usage patterns.

nodes.summary: React Spectrum 2 Tabs component can crash when overflow/collapse unmounts its internal TabListStateContext; use SegmentedControl + conditional rendering instead.
nodes.details: S2 horizontal Tabs on the Registrations page (/registrations) can enter an overflow/collapse path that unmounts the react-aria-components Tabs shell, leaving TabListStateContext null and causing 'Cannot read properties of null (reading selectedKey)' crashes. Replace with SegmentedControl + SegmentedControlItem (the established EMC pattern) paired with selectedTab state to conditionally render the three sections (Registrations, Campaigns, Sessions). This avoids the context unmounting issue entirely. See web-src/src/pages/Registrations/Registrations.tsx for the applied pattern.

nodes.summary: Production event publishing requires explicit user confirmation via AlertDialog before calling publishEvent; dev/stage builds skip this gate.
nodes.details: In EventForm.tsx, when ENVIRONMENT=prod, both handleComplete and executeSaveWithUrl paths funnel through requestPublishAfterUrlResolved, which opens a Spectrum 2 AlertDialog for user acceptance before invoking publishEvent. The extraPayload ref is cleared only on confirm or Cancel, not in onOpenChange, to preserve the payload if close handlers fire before onPrimaryAction executes. This pattern prevents accidental production event publication.

nodes.summary: Session location-time conflict validation must occur on both FE (inline UX + cost reduction) and BE (atomicity guard), with FE checking interval overlap via UTC millisecond conversion and BE as final arbiter.
nodes.details: SessionForm.tsx implements FE-side conflict detection by accepting allSessions prop, deriving hasLocationConflict via useMemo that converts form date/time to UTC milliseconds (reusing naiveDateTimeToUTCMillis + dateAndTimeToISO utilities) and scans for overlapping intervals on same locationId (currentStart < sEnd && currentEnd > sStart), excluding self in edit mode. This marks Location ComboBox isInvalid and blocks Save button. BE (events-service-platform PR #922) performs final DynamoDB scan validation. FE guard reduces unnecessary requests and narrows race-condition window; BE guard ensures atomicity. SessionsList threads allSessions through component hierarchy (SessionsListProps → SessionItemProps → SessionForm) for both add and edit forms; Sessions.tsx sources from existing state, no new fetches.

nodes.summary: Do not spread GET response into PUT body; construct narrow association payloads with only required fields plus timestamps.
nodes.details: In `web-src/src/services/api.ts`, `updateSpeakerInEvent` previously merged the full GET response (minus `creationTime`) into the PUT body, sending unintended fields to ESP. The corrected pattern: construct PUT payloads with only `speakerId`, `speakerType`, `ordinal` (from caller patch with GET fallbacks when omitted), plus `creationTime` and `modificationTime` from GET. This matches the documented ESP contract and the existing `updateSponsorInEvent` pattern. Callers like the Speakers dashboard may send partial patches (e.g., only `speakerId`); the service must fill missing association fields from the prior GET before PUT.

nodes.summary: Session form dirty-state tracking and unsaved-changes dialog: parent components receive `sessionHasOpenForm` prop to gate navigation; SessionForm detects dirty state and triggers callbacks; FormWizard integrates confirmation dialog before allowing navigation away.
nodes.details: The session management enhancement establishes a pattern for handling unsaved changes across the EventForm hierarchy. SessionManagementComponent tracks form state via `sessionHasOpenForm` prop and notifies parents of changes. SessionForm is responsible for detecting dirty state (form modifications) and invoking callbacks to signal this state upward. FormWizard consumes this signal and blocks navigation by rendering a confirmation dialog before allowing users to leave the form. This pattern ensures data loss prevention across nested form components without losing the ability to navigate intentionally. Apply this pattern to other multi-step forms in EMC that risk data loss on navigation.

nodes.summary: CSV export filename convention: prefix with event title and ISO datetime, sanitize user input, append .csv extension only at download time.
nodes.details: EMC attendee and campaign exports use a standardized filename pattern: `[event-title]_[YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS]` for attendees, `[event-title]_campaigns_[YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS]` for campaigns. The `utils/csvExport.ts` module provides `sanitizeFilename()` and `exportDatetime()` helpers to enforce this. Filenames are user-editable in the export dialog but must be sanitized before download; `.csv` extension is appended at download time, not stored in the user-facing field. This pattern applies across ExportDialog.tsx (attendee) and CampaignExportDialog (campaign tab).

nodes.summary: Parallel API queries for attendee status types are merged into a single result set; new status types require only type union updates and StatusBadge entries, not table/filter/export logic changes.
nodes.details: In EMC's Registrations page, attendee statuses (registered, waitlisted, declined) are fetched via parallel `?type=X` queries in `getAllEventAttendees()` (web-src/src/services/api.ts) and merged into a single `AttendeeStats` result. The `RegistrationStatus` type union (web-src/src/types/attendee.ts) controls which statuses exist. Adding a new status requires: (1) extending the `RegistrationStatus` union, (2) adding a `StatusBadge` variant entry (web-src/src/components/shared/StatusBadge.tsx), and (3) updating `AttendeeStats` interface. Table rendering, filtering, and CSV export are data-driven and automatically support new statuses without code changes.

nodes.summary: Sessions tab in Event Report uses lazy-loaded expandable rows to display per-session attendee lists, cross-referencing session-time attendees with event attendees for display names.
nodes.details: The Sessions registration tab (SessionsTab.tsx) implements a table with expandable rows that lazy-load attendee data via getSessionTimeAttendees(timeId) from GET /v1/session-times/{timeId}/attendees. Attendee display names are resolved by cross-referencing the session-time attendee list against the parent event's attendee roster. SessionTimeInfo type extends with attendeeCount, waitlistAttendeeCount, isFull fields. Expanded state resets when switching events to avoid stale data.

nodes.summary: Do not omit server modification time (mtime) when updating session-time API without page refresh; failure to persist and send mtime in consecutive calls triggers OptimisticLockExceptionError.
nodes.details: The session-time API endpoint requires the server's modification timestamp (mtime) to be stored after each response and included in subsequent PUT/PATCH requests. When session-time params are updated in-memory without a page refresh, the mtime must be extracted from the server response and cached in component state (e.g., Sessions.tsx) so it is available for the next API call. Omitting mtime causes the server to reject the update as a stale write. Additionally, ensure POST is only called once during session creation; subsequent updates must use PUT/PATCH with the cached mtime to avoid duplicate session-time records.

nodes.summary: RichTextEditor export must use getSemanticHTML() to produce portable <ul>/<ol> instead of Quill's internal data-list markup; normalize NBSP variants on load/export for API consistency.
nodes.details: In web-src/src/components/shared/RichTextEditor.tsx, call getSemanticHTML() instead of root.innerHTML when exporting editor content so that bullet lists serialize as semantic <ul> and numbered lists as <ol>, not Quill 2's internal <ol data-list="…"> format. This ensures stored HTML is portable across APIs and event copy systems. Additionally, normalize all NBSP variants ( ,  , \u00A0) to regular spaces during both load (via clipboard.convert + setContents) and export, and align onChange / prop sync comparisons on the normalized form to prevent re-apply loops and caret jumps. Restrict formats whitelist to toolbar capabilities (bold, italic, underline, strike, list, indent, align, link) to prevent pasted content from retaining unwanted styling (color, background, font, size).

nodes.summary: Do not omit detailPagePath from event PUT payloads; instead, use dataFilters to toggle submittable: true when title changes, coordinating with backend OpenAPI spec updates.
nodes.details: When updating an event via ESL PUT, detailPagePath was previously omitted because the backend marked it read-only. However, title changes require a new detailPagePath (new DA page). The fix: in useEventFormSave.ts, call dataFilters to set detailPagePath.submittable = true before the PUT, and detect title changes to trigger the DA page path dialog. This requires coordinated backend changes to the OpenAPI spec to allow the field in PUT requests. The anti-pattern is assuming a read-only field can never be submitted; instead, use conditional submittability flags in dataFilters based on business logic (e.g., title mutation).

nodes.summary: Event form boolean toggles (showSponsors) default to true on creation and use ?? true fallback on load to handle omitted API fields.
nodes.details: When restoring or initializing event form state, boolean visibility toggles like showSponsors must default to true in EventFormContext and use nullish coalescing (?? true) in eventFormMappers.ts during load to gracefully handle API responses that omit the field. The payload serialization via buildEventPayload and EVENT_DATA_FILTER already includes the field when set; the mapper ensures the UI layer has a consistent default. This pattern applies to other optional boolean fields controlling detail-page visibility.

nodes.summary: EMC dark mode uses system prefers-color-scheme via usePreferredColorScheme hook, syncs React Spectrum 2 colorScheme prop, and defines semantic CSS tokens (--emc-field-*, --emc-event-form-shell-bg) that mirror compiled S2 Field colors (dark #111 fill, #444 border) under both @media and html[data-color-scheme] selectors for hydration safety.
nodes.details: The usePreferredColorScheme hook (web-src/src/hooks/usePreferredColorScheme.ts) subscribes to matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') and sets document.documentElement.dataset.colorScheme, which is passed to S2Provider colorScheme prop in App/AuthGate/RBACGate. index.css defines light :root defaults and dark @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) overrides for both legacy --spectrum-global-* and new semantic tokens (--emc-field-bg, --emc-field-border, --emc-field-focus-ring). Tokens are duplicated under html[data-color-scheme='dark'] selector to ensure first paint and post-effect hydration alignment. Custom controls (Quill RTE via .rte-field-shell, Google Places venue field via .emc-field-like) suppress UA outline and use :focus-visible for keyboard focus rings while relying on border changes for mouse focus, matching S2 behavior. designSystem.ts SURFACES enum (shell/card/format-dialog) centralizes surface-level background tokens.

nodes.summary: EMC is a frontend-only ExC Shell SPA with no backend repo; all mutations and queries call external Adobe APIs (ESP, ESL) directly through a centralized ApiService with caching, validation, and dry-run support.
nodes.details: EMC (web-src/src/) is a React 18 + TypeScript + React Spectrum S2 SPA deployed via Adobe App Builder. There is no backend in this repo. All API calls route through services/api.ts (ApiService) and cachedApi wrapper: GET requests use 10s caching with request dedup and pattern-based invalidation; all mutations require input validation via validateString()/validateObject() before dispatch; all fetch calls pass through safeFetch() with ALLOWED_HOSTS validation. Two external backends: Adobe ESP (events/series/speakers endpoints) and ESL (lifecycle/venues/attendees). Auth uses Bearer token (IMS in prod, dev token locally) + x-gw-ims-org-id header. Dry-run mode available via apiService.enableDryRun(). Form state (EventForm, SeriesForm) persists to sessionStorage with debounced auto-save; multi-step FormWizard uses useEventFormComponent hook lifecycle (onGatherPayload, onAfterSave, onLoadResponse, validate) for step registration.

nodes.summary: ENVIRONMENT variable is baked into the bundle at build time to control API tier routing (dev/stage/prod), not set at runtime.
nodes.details: The EMC frontend uses the ENVIRONMENT variable (dev/stage/prod) set during the build process to determine which API endpoints the app calls at runtime. This is configured in .env and baked into the bundle, not read dynamically. The mapping is: dev → dev cluster, stage → events-service-platform-stage.adobe.io + events-service-layer-stage.adobe.io, prod → events-service-platform.adobe.io + events-service-layer.adobe.io. Deploy commands (npm run deploy:dev/stage/prod) handle setting ENVIRONMENT before build. This pattern prevents runtime environment mismatches and ensures API tier consistency across a deployment.

nodes.summary: EMC centralizes all API calls through a singleton ApiService class with consistent error handling, authentication management, and mock-to-real API switching via config.json action URLs.
nodes.details: All external API calls route through ApiService.callAction<T>(actionName, params, method) in /web-src/src/services/api.ts. Authentication is set once via apiService.setAuthHeaders(token, org) and applied to all requests. Backend URLs are configured via apiService.setActionUrls(urls) from config.json, enabling mock-to-real switching without code changes: remove mock import, update the method to call this.callAction('actionName'), and add the URL to config.json actions object. Mock data lives in /web-src/src/mocks/ as TypeScript modules exporting both data and Promise-returning functions (with 300ms delay to simulate latency). This pattern decouples frontend from backend readiness and enables parallel development.

nodes.summary: EMC caching and throttling utilities follow a three-layer request pattern (cache → pending → new request) with function-name-based key generation, 10-second default TTL, pattern-based invalidation, and automatic cache busting on mutations.
nodes.details: The `apiCache` utility in `web-src/src/services/cacheUtils.ts` implements request deduplication and memoization via an IIFE module pattern. All GET operations in `cachedApi` (in `web-src/src/services/api.ts` ~line 1680+) are wrapped with `apiCache.get()`, and mutations automatically invalidate related cache entries by pattern matching (e.g., `cachedApi.updateEvent()` invalidates `getEvent()` and `getEventsList()` caches). URL-based caches use `fetchThrottledMemoizedText` and `fetchThrottledMemoizedJSON` with configurable TTL. Debounce (300ms for search) and throttle (100-200ms for scroll/resize) utilities follow the same patterns documented in `throttling.md`. Cache can be inspected via `getCacheStats()` and cleared via `clearCache()` or `invalidateCache(pattern)`.

nodes.summary: EMC frontend uses centralized design tokens (LAYOUT_DIMENSIONS, COLORS, Z_INDEX, pre-composed style objects) imported from `/web-src/src/styles/designSystem.ts` to enforce UI consistency and maintainability.
nodes.details: All layout dimensions (GNAV_HEIGHT=56px, ACTION_BAR_HEIGHT=60px, SIDE_NAV_WIDTH=240px), colors (COLORS.ADOBE_RED, COLORS.GRAY_*), z-index layering (Z_INDEX.MODAL=600, Z_INDEX.GNAV=1000), and common style patterns (STICKY_GNAV_STYLES, FIXED_ACTION_BAR_STYLES, SCROLLABLE_CONTENT_STYLES) must be imported from designSystem.ts rather than hardcoded. Helper functions like createFixedHeightStyle() and createActionBarPadding() compute viewport-relative dimensions. Button state colors (BUTTON_HOVER_OVERLAY, BUTTON_ACTIVE_OVERLAY) are defined but legacy—Spectrum defaults are preferred. This centralizes all UI constants and prevents drift across components.

nodes.summary: EMC App Builder development uses Experience Cloud Shell devMode with deployed backend + local frontend hot reload for IMS-authenticated development; backend changes require `aio app deploy --actions` redeploy.
nodes.details: The recommended development workflow is: (1) deploy backend actions once via `aio app deploy`, (2) access frontend via `https://experience.adobe.com/?devMode=true#/@ORG/APP-ID` which enables hot reload of `web-src/` changes and automatic IMS token injection, (3) for backend changes, redeploy via `aio app deploy --actions`. The app.config.yaml annotation `require-adobe-auth: true` ensures Adobe API Gateway validates IMS tokens before actions execute. Frontend receives IMS data via `runtime.on('ready', ({ imsOrg, imsToken, imsProfile }))` and must pass tokens in API calls; developers should never manually manage tokens. Local-only mode (`aio app run --local`) is for action debugging only, not production-like IMS testing.

nodes.summary: Dev token mode is explicitly opt-in via URL parameter and host allowlist; never interferes with real IMS in Experience Cloud Shell.
nodes.details: Dev token UI and localStorage token usage are only active when URL contains `?devtokenmode=true` AND host is in allowlist (checked via `isDevTokenModeEnabled()` in env.ts). Two separate bootstrap paths exist: `bootstrapInExcShell()` always uses real IMS token and completely bypasses dev token system; `bootstrapStandalone()` uses dev token from localStorage only when dev token mode is enabled. This dual-path design ensures dev tokens never interfere with production shell deployments.

nodes.summary: Dev token system is gated by both URL query parameter (?devtokenmode=true) and host allowlist (localhost or approved dev instances); without the parameter, the UI button is hidden and stored tokens are not used for API calls.
nodes.details: The dev token feature in EMC requires two conditions to be active: (1) the URL must include ?devtokenmode=true and (2) the host must be localhost or an approved dev instance (e.g., 14257-emc-dev.adobeio-static.net). When both conditions are met, the Dev Token button appears in the top-right UI and API calls use the stored token via tokenStorage.getValidToken(). When running in Adobe Experience Cloud Shell, the real IMS token is automatically used instead and the dev token button never appears. API calls should use constructRequestHeaders(token) and safeFetch() helpers to inject the token into request headers.

nodes.summary: EMC dev token system uses two-path bootstrap architecture: ExC Shell path (real IMS) vs. standalone path (dev token), with dev token activation gated by both hostname allowlist AND ?devtokenmode=true URL parameter.
nodes.details: The dev token system is never active in Experience Cloud Shell (bootstrapInExcShell() path); it only activates in standalone mode (bootstrapStandalone()) when both hostname is in DEV_TOKEN_ALLOWED_HOSTNAMES (localhost, 127.0.0.1, or specific adobeio-static.net subdomains) AND URL contains ?devtokenmode=true. The isDevTokenModeEnabled() function in web-src/src/config/env.ts enforces this dual gate. Dev token button visibility, token storage use in ApiService.getAuthToken(), and useDevToken hook all depend on this check. This ensures dev tokens never leak into production/staging deployments and cannot interfere with real IMS sessions in the shell.

nodes.summary: Event Form uses 4-step wizard structure where Step 1 groups 5 logical components (format, tags, info, dates, venue) rather than separating into individual steps; this matches v1 reference and improves UX.
nodes.details: The EventForm wizard in EMC follows a deliberate 4-step structure (not 8) where Step 1 contains EventFormatComponent, Tags, Event Info, Date/Time, and Venue components as logical sub-sections. This pattern groups related fields (e.g., all basic event metadata in Step 1) while keeping the overall flow concise. Step 2 handles Speakers/Hosts, Step 3 handles images, Step 4 handles RSVP/status. When implementing new event forms or extending this wizard, maintain this grouping: do not split Step 1 into separate steps unless UX research shows users abandon multi-step forms at >6 steps. The FormWizard shared component manages progress tracking and navigation across all steps.

nodes.summary: EMC frontend organizes event form as 13 modular components under EventForm/ directory, each owning a logical section (venue, speakers, agenda, etc.), composed by EventForm.tsx wizard container.
nodes.details: The EventForm/ directory contains 13 specialized components (EventFormatComponent, EventInfoComponent, VenueComponent, SpeakersComponent, SponsorsComponent, AgendaComponent, EventImagesComponent, ProfilesComponent, RegistrationConfigComponent, RegistrationFieldsComponent, PageMetadataComponent, plus index.ts barrel export) that are composed into a multi-step wizard by the parent EventForm.tsx container. Each component owns a logical domain (e.g., VenueComponent handles Google Places integration, SpeakersComponent manages speaker CRUD, RegistrationFieldsComponent configures RSVP form fields). This modular decomposition enables independent testing, reuse, and maintenance of form sections. The barrel export (index.ts) centralizes imports for the parent wizard.

nodes.summary: EMC uses environment-specific Google Places API keys (DEV_/STAGE_/PROD_ prefixes) loaded from .env, with automatic selection based on runtime environment.
nodes.details: The application loads Google Places API via loadGooglePlacesAPI() utility in VenueComponent on mount. API keys are stored in .env as DEV_GOOGLE_PLACES_API, STAGE_GOOGLE_PLACES_API, and PROD_GOOGLE_PLACES_API; the runtime automatically selects the correct key based on environment. Each key should be restricted by HTTP referrer (localhost:* for dev, *.stage.adobe.com/* for staging, *.adobe.com/* for prod). The Places API call requests only specific fields: place_id, name, formatted_address, geometry, utc_offset_minutes. VenueComponent auto-populates venue name, full address, lat/lng, Place ID, and GMT offset from the response, but the address field remains user-editable.

nodes.summary: RBAC permission gating uses wildcard-matching permission strings (resource:access format) with fallback to domain-only permissions when role fetch returns 403, and gates UI elements via useHasPermission hooks and filterEvents/filterSeries helpers.
nodes.details: Permissions are stored as Set<RBACPermission> in GroupContext and checked via useHasPermission(resource, access) or useRBACFilter helpers. Wildcard matching order: *:* → exact → resource:* → *:access. When GET /v1/roles/{roleId} returns 403, frontend falls back to event:*, series:*, session:*, cloud:*, config:*, integration:* (all domain actions visible, admin UI hidden). GroupContext increments groupVersion on group switch to trigger dashboard re-fetches; role is resolved before groupVersion bump to prevent race conditions. UI elements (TopNav tabs, Home cards, OverviewDashboard stat cards) are conditionally rendered using canReadEvents/canReadSeries/canReadClouds derived from useHasPermission. API service injects x-adobe-esp-group-id header for ESP requests when activeGroupId is set.

nodes.summary: EMC migrated from sidebar to top navigation (gnav) layout; TopNav component in SideBar.tsx with UserPanel compact mode; App.tsx grid changed from ['sidebar', 'content'] to ['header', 'content'] with rows ['auto', '1fr'].
nodes.details: The layout shift encodes a durable architectural pattern: (1) SideBar.tsx was repurposed as TopNav with horizontal nav items and brand logo on left, user panel on right; (2) UserPanel.tsx gained a `compact` prop that hides email/org and reduces avatar size for header context; (3) App.tsx grid layout changed from 2-column sidebar model to 2-row header model with grid areas ['header', 'content'] and rows ['auto', '1fr']; (4) Navigation links use `.nav-link` class with bottom border (3px solid transparent) for active state, not background highlight; (5) Content area must have `gridArea='content'` and overflow scroll enabled. This pattern is reusable for any future layout refactors and clarifies the component responsibility split.

nodes.summary: IMS user context must be threaded as a prop through component tree (App → UserPanel, SideBar); UserPanel displays profile data with graceful fallback when IMS profile unavailable.
nodes.details: The UserPanel component receives an `ims` prop containing `{ profile?: IMSProfile, org?: string, token?: string }` where IMSProfile has `userId`, `name`, `email`. Components extract user context via optional chaining (e.g., `ims.profile?.name || 'Guest'`). When `ims.profile` is absent, UserPanel renders 'Not Connected' state. This pattern establishes the contract for how IMS data flows through the EMC frontend: App.tsx passes `ims` to both UserPanel and SideBar, and any component needing user context receives the same IMS object structure. Token is never rendered; user ID is truncated in UI for privacy.

nodes.summary: RSVP registration payloads must include `requiresSxswTicket` flag and implicit consent via `contactMethods` field; sanitize HTML in form text/textarea inputs and enforce RSVP limit column as maxlength constraint.
nodes.details: When submitting event-attendee payloads for RSVP, include `requiresSxswTicket` boolean when SXSW ticket filter applies (#140). Implicit consent for new registrations is recorded via the `contactMethods` field in the payload (MWPW-194036, #126). In events-form block (event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js), sanitize HTML in text and textarea inputs (#110) and honor the RSVP limit column value as the `maxlength` attribute constraint. These patterns ensure consistent registration data shape and prevent XSS while respecting capacity limits.

nodes.summary: Event-attendee payload fields must be explicitly listed in EVENT_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER to be sent to ESL's addAttendeeToEvent endpoint.
nodes.details: The EVENT_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER in event-libs/v1/utils/data-utils.js acts as an allowlist for which form fields are included in the event-attendee payload sent to ESL. New checkbox or form fields (e.g., requiresSxswTicket, shareInfoWithPartners) must be added to this filter in getEventAttendeePayload() to be transmitted. Additionally, when gating form fields via rsvp-form-fields metadata in events-form.js, new sheet fields must be listed in the visible array to render; unlisted fields are silently dropped.

nodes.summary: Sessions Hub text search is scoped to title, speaker names, and tag labels; descriptions excluded by default unless `search-include-description` block class is set.
nodes.details: The filterSessions function in event-libs/v1/blocks/sessions-hub/sessions-hub.js implements a three-field search pattern: title, speaker (first/last/full-name substring), and tag labels are matched case-insensitively against trimmed queries ≥2 characters. Session descriptions are intentionally excluded from the default search scope to reduce noise; marketers can opt into description matching by adding the `search-include-description` block class. A query of 1 character or whitespace-only does not filter by text, leaving all sessions visible subject to tab/tag filters. When a qualifying search returns zero results, the no-results UI (role="status", aria-live="polite") is shown and the session grid is hidden.

nodes.summary: RSVP form `limit` field is applied only to text inputs and textareas via HTML `maxlength` attribute; invalid values are logged but not thrown, and missing/empty limits are silently omitted.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js, the `limit` column from RSVP form JSON (table export) is parsed as a positive integer and applied as the `maxlength` HTML attribute only on elements created by `createInput` and `createTextArea` helpers. Invalid limit values are logged via `window.lana` without throwing errors; this graceful degradation ensures backward compatibility. Selects, checkboxes, and other input types do not receive the `limit` field. Configs without a `limit` column or with empty/invalid values behave identically to pre-feature versions (no `maxlength` attribute).

nodes.summary: Use CSS Grid subgrid on agenda list items to align time-track widths and vertical dividers across multi-row schedule columns.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/event-agenda/event-agenda.css, apply a two-column template (`minmax(215px, max-content) 1fr`) to `.column` and use `subgrid` on `.agenda-list-item` so all rows within a column inherit the same track widths. Replace per-row flex dividers with `border-inline-start` on the title cell to maintain vertical rule alignment. This pattern ensures consistent time-column width and divider positioning across variable-height agenda items without per-row layout recalculation.

nodes.summary: Implicit consent on RSVP is recorded by populating the existing contactMethods array when consent UI shows messaging only (no checkboxes), sourced from authored implicit-consent metadata.
nodes.details: When an RSVP form has consent messaging but no explicit checkboxes, call parseImplicitConsentChannels() to extract channel names from the implicit-consent metadata (checked in order: fragment <meta>, query param implicitConsent/implicit_consent, or page meta), then apply applyImplicitContactMethodsToPayload() to inject those channels into the attendee payload's contactMethods array before submitForm validation. This reuses the existing getBaseAttendeePayload / ESL pipeline without adding new attendee attributes. The metadata resolution and payload mutation happen in events-form.js after loadFragment but before API submission.

nodes.summary: Do not pass user-supplied HTML strings through Milo's createTag() when building modal content; use plain-text helpers to avoid unintended focusable elements.
nodes.details: In profile-cards, speaker `title` field was passed directly to `createTag()`, which interprets strings as HTML. This caused markup like `<a>` tags to render before the modal's intended first focusable (`h2.card-name`), breaking Milo's `FOCUSABLES` selector and causing incorrect focus-visible styling on modal open. Solution: extract `modalJobTitlePlainText()` helper and use it exclusively in `buildModalContent()` for `.card-title` elements. Grid card rendering (which does not use modals) remains unchanged. Mirror Milo's `FOCUSABLES` selector in unit tests to verify focus order.

nodes.summary: Promotional content resolution follows a two-tier fallback pattern: prefer custom-attributes meta tag (promotionalItems) for direct fragment URLs; fall back to legacy promotional-items meta + promotional-content.json fetch if custom-attributes absent.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/promotional-content/promotional-content.js, getPromotionalContent() now checks for fragment URLs in the custom-attributes meta tag (attribute 'promotionalItems') as the primary path. If absent or empty, it invokes getLegacyPromotionalContent() which reads the promotional-items meta tag and fetches promotional-content.json to resolve fragment paths. Both paths normalize to a flat array of fragment URLs before the unified fragment-loading loop. Use nullish-coalescing (?? []) and optional chaining (?.) to guard against null/undefined returns from either path, preventing crashes on pages with neither meta tag present.

nodes.summary: Session registration UI follows a three-state model (Registered/Waitlisted, Able to Register, Blocked) with explicit predicates for each state; SessionTimeFull responses must be read from body, not just HTTP status.
nodes.details: In `event-libs/v1/blocks/sessions-hub/sessions-hub.js`, the per-card CTA must implement exactly three states: (1) Registered/Waitlisted badge (blue, shows checkmark + text from `waitlist-cta-text` dictionary key, hover swaps to unregister action), (2) Able-to-register button (direct `registerForSessionTime` API call, no modal), (3) Blocked button (disabled `.sh-btn-blocked`, labeled from `Registration unavailable` dictionary key). Use the pure predicate `isSessionRegistrationBlocked({ isEventWaitlisted, isEventClosed, inviteOnlyBlocked })` to determine blocked state. For session-time registration responses, read `resp.body.data.registrationStatus === 'waitlisted'` to distinguish waitlist from full registration (2xx with waitlist status must set `session.isWaitlisted`, not `isRegistered`). Use `isSessionTimeFullError(resp)` helper to detect SessionTimeFull errors by checking `error.code | errorCode | error | type | message` fields defensively. Event-level waitlist state (`rsvpData.registrationStatus === 'waitlisted'`) blocks all per-card registration; event-closed state (computed from `isFull && !allowWaitlisting`, accepting both boolean and string `'true'`) also blocks. Banner visibility: keep visible for waitlisted users (only hide when `isEventRegistered === true`), render `sh-banner-waitlist-msg` paragraph with `getEventWaitlistBannerMessage(manager, { eventTitle })` helper from `dictionary-manager.js`.

nodes.summary: Invite-only events without a valid campaign parameter must block RSVP UI and show a shared dictionary-driven message across all event blocks (decorate, events-form, sessions-hub).
nodes.details: When an invite-only event is opened without a valid `campaign` URL parameter, the RSVP flow is blocked. Use `dictionaryManager.getInviteOnlyNoCampaignMessage()` to fetch the user-facing message from the dictionary sheet. In sessions-hub, compute `inviteOnlyBlocked` after `await dictionaryManager.initialize()`, then replace the sticky Register CTA and per-card event-registration buttons with the status message. Guard all click handlers and sessionStorage-deferred modal opens to prevent RSVP submission. Apply CSS classes `.sh-banner-invite-only-msg` and `.sh-invite-only-msg` for styling. This pattern ensures parity across decorate.js, events-form.js, and sessions-hub.js.

nodes.summary: Mobile-rider block lifecycle: dispose prior player instance before re-embed, use single streamend listener, and trigger timing-framework liveStreamEnd flag to unblock next schedule item.
nodes.details: The mobile-rider block (event-libs/v1/blocks/mobile-rider/mobile-rider.js) must call dispose() on any existing player instance before injecting a new one to prevent stacking listeners and resource leaks. Register only one streamend listener per session; do not re-attach on re-embed. When a stream ends, set liveStreamEnd=true in the timing-framework worker (worker-traditional.js) so the next schedule item triggers immediately instead of waiting for toggleTime. This pattern ensures clean player teardown and prevents schedule deadlock in concurrent-video scenarios.

nodes.summary: Phone field validation in RSVP forms uses a code-level default pattern before sheet-driven config is available, enabling safe rollout across environments.
nodes.details: The events-form block (event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js) validates businessPhone and mobilePhone fields with a built-in regex pattern as a fallback. This pattern-based default exists because the RSVP config sheets (experiencecloud and creativecloud) are shared across environments and cannot be updated atomically with code. The pattern is temporary: once the sheet is updated, the code-level default is removed in a follow-up PR. This pattern prevents validation gaps during the transition window and should be replicated for any future phone or pattern-based field validations that depend on external config.

nodes.summary: Invite-only events gate RSVP behind `inviteOnly` flag and campaign URL param; replace button with text message rather than disable.
nodes.details: The invite-only RSVP feature gates registration on two conditions: (1) an `inviteOnly` event flag from the backend, and (2) a campaign URL parameter. When both conditions are met, the RSVP button is replaced with a text message instead of being disabled. This pattern prevents accidental user confusion and clarifies that the event is not available for self-service registration. Check `event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js` for the gating logic and button replacement implementation.

nodes.summary: Resolve human-readable tag labels from chimera API via getCaasTags() utility rather than deriving them client-side from CaaS tag IDs.
nodes.details: When displaying CaaS tag IDs (e.g. `caas:events/type/deep-dive`) in the sessions-hub block, call the existing `getCaasTags()` utility from `esp-controller.js` to fetch tag metadata and use the `.title` field for display labels. This ensures multi-word tags render correctly (e.g. "Deep Dive" instead of "Deep-dive"). Fetch `getCaasTags()` in parallel with `resolveRegistrationState()` at block init time; use `null` as a silent fallback if the fetch fails. This pattern applies to any frontend block that needs to display CaaS tag labels.

nodes.summary: Do not rely on :focus:not(:focus-visible) CSS to suppress focus rings when Milo's getModal uses .focus({ focusVisible: true }) — the flag forces :focus-visible to match regardless of input method.
nodes.details: Milo's getModal helper focuses the first FOCUSABLE element using .focus({ focusVisible: true }), which explicitly forces :focus-visible to match even on programmatic focus. CSS rules like :focus:not(:focus-visible) cannot suppress this ring. Instead, ensure the first FOCUSABLE in modal DOM order is an element where outline: none is already applied (e.g., a heading with tabindex="0"), or add outline: none to the element that will receive initial focus. In profile-cards/profile-cards.js, the fix was to add tabindex="0" to the card-name h2 in buildModalContent so it precedes social links in focus order, and the existing .card-name:focus { outline: none; } rule suppresses the ring.

nodes.summary: Do not call closeModal() without passing the modal DOM element argument; it causes TypeError when modal.js tries to read the element's id property.
nodes.details: In sessions-hub.js, closeModal() requires a modal DOM element parameter. Previously, closeModal() was invoked without arguments, causing 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')' in Milo's modal.js. The fix: capture the dialog element returned by getModal() and pass it to all closeModal() calls. This pattern applies to any Milo modal integration — always bind the element reference before invoking close operations.

nodes.summary: Branch parameter in milolibs query must be whitelisted to alphanumeric, underscore, and hyphen characters; reject all other input to prevent injection or malformed routing.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/utils/utils.js, the milolibs branch parameter is validated against the regex /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/ before use. This whitelist prevents injection attacks and ensures branch names conform to expected naming conventions. Any branch parameter containing special characters (e.g., slashes, dots, semicolons) must be rejected at parse time, not passed through to downstream routing or library resolution logic.

nodes.summary: Invite-only events require a valid campaign URL parameter (?campaign=) to enable RSVP; gating occurs at button-disable and form-build stages with dictionary-driven error messaging.
nodes.details: When an event has inviteOnly=true, RSVP is blocked unless a valid campaign ID is present in the URL query string. Validation uses getValidCampaignIdFromUrl() (utils/utils.js) against CAMPAIGN_ID_PATTERN (utils/constants.js). Gating is enforced in two places: (1) updateRSVPButtonState in decorate.js disables the button early via setCtaState('inviteOnlyNoCampaign'), and (2) events-form.js handleProfile blocks form construction entirely and renders an error message keyed to rsvp-invite-only-no-campaign-cta-text in the dictionary. The campaign ID is then passed to submitForm for server-side validation.

nodes.summary: Detect session description truncation via DOM layout (scrollHeight vs clientHeight) rather than character limits; re-sync on filter, expand/collapse, font load, and resize events.
nodes.details: In sessions-hub.js, replace fixed-character truncation logic with dynamic overflow detection: compare element.scrollHeight > element.clientHeight to determine if text is truncated. Export syncSessionDescriptionsOverflow() and call it after filter changes, expand/collapse toggles, fonts ready (via document.fonts.ready), and ResizeObserver triggers. This ensures descriptions adapt to actual layout constraints (viewport, font metrics, container width) rather than hardcoded thresholds. Apply the same sync pattern to the conflict modal: defer modal close until registration completes, show pending state on confirm button and option elements, and restore UI on failure.

nodes.summary: Sessions-hub auto-registration integrates RSVP form submission through events-form block; chrono-box conditionally suppresses first schedule item when no conditions match.
nodes.details: The sessions-hub block now triggers auto-registration by delegating form submission to the events-form block rather than handling RSVP directly. This pattern centralizes form field validation and payload preparation in events-form. Additionally, chrono-box (timing-framework) implements conditional rendering: the first schedule item is skipped if no time-condition rules match, preventing empty or placeholder schedule displays. Both patterns live in event-libs/v1/blocks/ and should be followed when extending RSVP or schedule rendering flows.

nodes.summary: Form field names must be trimmed before matching against visibility/required metadata arrays to prevent silent field filtering due to whitespace.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js, the createForm() function must call trim() on field names from the form config before using them in visible.includes(f.field) and required.includes(lowkey.field) checks. Untrimmed field names (e.g. 'shareInfoWithPartners\n') will fail to match the rsvp-form-fields metadata arrays, causing fields to be silently filtered out and not rendered. Apply trim() consistently when setting data-field-id and input id attributes as well to maintain alignment between config, metadata, and DOM.

nodes.summary: Auto-session-registration logic moved from sessions-hub to events-form block via BlockMediator; isAutoRegistrationEnabled check must occur before form submission to avoid false positives.
nodes.details: The auto-registration flow is now owned by the events-form block, which receives session context via BlockMediator. The isAutoRegistrationEnabled flag must be evaluated at form-submission time (not at block-init time) to correctly detect when a user is already registered in a conflicting session. See esp-controller.js and events-form.js for the BlockMediator handoff pattern and the timing of the registration-state check.

nodes.summary: Profile card images without altText must be marked decorative with alt="" and role="presentation" for screen reader accessibility.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/profile-cards/profile-cards.js, member images are conditionally rendered: if altText exists, use it as the alt attribute; if altText is absent, set alt="" and role="presentation" to signal to assistive technology that the image is decorative and should be skipped. Social icons retain their platform-specific alt text (e.g., alt="${platform} logo") and are unaffected. This pattern ensures WCAG 2.1 Level A compliance for images that carry no semantic meaning.

nodes.summary: Profile card heading hierarchy and typography must align with Figma design specs: card names render as h2 (not h3), descriptions use Body/L (18px/27px), and modal focus outlines are suppressed.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/profile-cards/, all render paths (decorateContent, decorateContentSimple, buildModalContent) must output card names as `<h2>` elements, not h3. Card description text (`.card-desc`) must use CSS custom properties `--type-body-l-size` and `--type-body-l-lh` (18px/27px) instead of `--type-body-xs-size` (14px/21px). Section heading h2 selectors must be scoped to `.profile-cards > div:first-child h2` to prevent style bleed to card-level h2s. Modal overlays must suppress the browser default focus outline on `.profile-cards-modal .card-name` with `outline: none;` to match Figma design intent. These constraints apply to both card view and modal render modes.

nodes.summary: Do not fall back to rendering the first schedule item when no conditions are satisfied; instead return null and let the timer continue polling for a future match.
nodes.details: In timing-framework workers (worker.js, worker-traditional.js), `getStartScheduleItemByToggleTime` must return `null` rather than falling back to schedule root when no item's toggle conditions are met. `initializeSchedule` should set `currentScheduleItem` to `null` (no render) while keeping `nextScheduleItem` at the first item so polling continues. `runTimer` must not call `getFirstScheduleItem()` as a fallback—if nothing qualifies, nothing is sent. This prevents chrono-box from rendering stale or incorrect content when all toggleTimes are in the future or unmet. `validateSchedulePosition` in worker.js handles cases where authoritative server time disagrees with wall-clock fast-path.

nodes.summary: Mock external Milo library imports in unit tests by providing local implementations and redirecting miloLibs via setEventConfig rather than relying on live CDN URLs.
nodes.details: When bento-cards and event-map blocks dynamically import Milo utilities (decorateButtons, createTag) from http://main--milo--adobecom.aem.live/libs/..., those imports fail in isolated test environments. Solution: create local mock modules in test/unit/blocks/{block}/mocks/libs/utils/ that export the needed functions, then call setEventConfig({ miloLibs: mockPath }) in each test's beforeEach to redirect the import resolution. This pattern avoids flaky network-dependent tests and ensures deterministic test behavior. Applied to bento-cards.test.js and event-map.test.js.

nodes.summary: profile-cards block supports a `modal` variant that renders full profile content in a Milo modal on card interaction, with hover elevation styling and responsive image constraints (max 385px width).
nodes.details: The profile-cards block in event-libs/v1/blocks/profile-cards/ now accepts a `modal` variant class that triggers Milo modal rendering for profile details. The variant applies hover elevation styling via CSS and enforces a 385px maximum width constraint on modal images. This pattern applies to both metadata-driven cards (from ESP) and static-authored cards, maintaining responsive behavior across viewport sizes. Implementation spans profile-cards.js (modal trigger logic), profile-cards.css (elevation + image constraints), and corresponding test fixtures.

nodes.summary: Chrono-box reparenting must only strip placeholder nodes outside the host element; in-host structure must be preserved to avoid breaking internal layout.
nodes.details: When chrono-box reparents content from fragments, the cleanup logic in chrono-box.js must filter placeholder removal to nodes that sit outside the chrono-box host container. Stripping in-host placeholders breaks the component's internal DOM structure. This applies to both initial fragment loads and schedule replacement scenarios. See commit `fix/chrono-box-reparent-in-host-only` and expanded test coverage in chrono-box.test.js.

nodes.summary: Chrono-box modal deep-link reliability: defer init resolution until loadFragment completes, then dispatch modal:open with deduplication and polling fallback.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/chrono-box/chrono-box.js, when pathToFragment is present, the block's init Promise must not resolve until loadFragment succeeds or fails. After fragment injection, poll for a[data-modal-hash] matching the URL hash (two rAFs + up to 12 frames), then call dispatchModalOpenOnceForHash which skips if the target already has .dialog-modal or if an identical hash was dispatched within 350ms. This deduplication window prevents duplicate modal:open events from concurrent worker ticks or Milo loadArea re-runs. Non-modal hash scrolling is not re-invoked post-fragment; rely on nested Milo loadArea for scroll behavior.

nodes.summary: Do not explicitly remove() nodes that remain within the chrono-box host during reparenting; rely on innerHTML clearing for in-host reorders to avoid redundant teardown.
nodes.details: chrono-box reparent cleanup must distinguish between nodes moved outside the host (which require explicit remove()) and nodes reordered within the subtree (which will be cleared by the next innerHTML swap). Guard orphan removal with `!chronoBoxEl.contains(node) && node.isConnected` in cleanupChronoBoxOutboundNodes. Calling remove() on in-host nodes triggers unnecessary teardown and diverges from the single-shot slot-clearing behavior. See event-libs/v1/blocks/chrono-box/chrono-box.js and corresponding unit test for the guard pattern.

nodes.summary: Do not call loadFragment with empty or missing pathToFragment; it resolves to the current document and can cause unbounded recursion when the page contains another chrono-box.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/chrono-box/chrono-box.js, normalize pathToFragment as a trimmed string and treat missing or non-string values as empty. When pathToFragment is empty, clear the block (innerHTML = ''), remove fixed height, revoke any worker blob URL, and skip the loadFragment call entirely. Passing an empty href to loadFragment causes it to fetch and inject the full current page, which may contain another chrono-box instance, leading to recursive reloads.

nodes.summary: chrono-box fragment swaps must clean up out-of-subtree reparented nodes via MutationObserver + teardown hooks, not just innerHTML clearing.
nodes.details: When Milo sticky-section and similar code re-parent DOM nodes (e.g. sections) outside the chrono-box subtree, clearing innerHTML alone does not remove them. Use MutationObserver (started before loadFragment, drained on swap via takeRecords()) to track same-turn reparents. On swap, dispatch chrono-box:before-swap event, run registered teardowns via registerChronoBoxOutboundCleanup(), remove reparented nodes, then remove [data-chrono-box-teleport] matches. Assign data-chrono-box-instance on the host element to enable author hooks. Optional ?chronoDebug=1 query param logs worker and fragment diagnostics.

nodes.summary: Do not assume social icon sources have uniform shape; ESP metadata supplies objects while static authoring supplies DOM anchors—decorateSocialIcons must handle both.
nodes.details: After the static-authoring refactor, decorateSocialIcons was narrowed to accept only HTMLAnchorElement, causing ESP metadata-driven speakers' socialLinks (supplied as { link, serviceName } objects) to be silently skipped. The fix restores support for anchors, link objects, and string URLs: clone anchors with inherited attributes, createTag for metadata objects with aria-label derived from serviceName or platform detection. Also restore the socialLinks || socialMedia fallback chain when decorating. This pattern applies to any block accepting speaker/profile data from both static HTML and ESP metadata sources.

nodes.summary: Do not use consentId as the select value for consent dropdowns; use countryCode instead to avoid index mismatches when consent options are reordered or filtered.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js, the consent select element must use countryCode (not consentId) as its value attribute. Using consentId caused duplicate/mismatched lookups when the DOM order of consent options diverged from the array index. This pattern applies to any consent-selection UI that maps user selections back to a consent configuration array.

nodes.summary: Do not use non-unique identifiers (consentId) as HTML select option values when the same ID appears across multiple rows; use a unique key (countryCode) as value and store the non-unique ID in a data attribute.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js, the consent country selector was setting `select.value = consentId`, which caused HTML's native select behavior to match only the first option with that value, leading to wrong country pre-population when the consent-query-index contained duplicate consentIds across countries. The fix: set `select.value = countryCode` (unique per country), store `consentId` in `data-consent-id` attribute on each option, then retrieve it via `selectedOption.dataset.consentId` during form submission. This pattern applies to any multi-row lookup where a non-unique identifier must be preserved for payload submission but a unique key is needed for DOM selection.

nodes.summary: RSVP contactMethods field must not be spread directly from GET response into PUT payload; use prepareContactMethodsForPut helper to normalize shape.
nodes.details: The events-form block's RSVP submission was spreading the GET response contactMethods array directly into the PUT body, causing server-side validation failures when field shapes diverged between read and write contracts. The fix introduces a normalization step (prepareContactMethodsForPut in event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js) that maps the GET schema to the PUT schema before submission. This pattern applies to all ESP PUT operations: never assume GET and PUT payloads have identical field structures; always use a prepare* helper to bridge the contract gap.

nodes.summary: RSVP button and form 400-error handling must respect campaign capacity when ?campaign URL param is present and valid, falling back to event capacity otherwise, with campaign-specific error messages and UI state.
nodes.details: When a valid campaign ID is present in the URL (?campaign=...), use getCampaign() to fetch campaign capacity and apply it to both RSVP button state (updateRSVPButtonState in decorate.js) and form 400-error handling (buildErrorMsg and submit handler in events-form.js). If campaign fetch fails or campaign ID is invalid (validate via CAMPAIGN_ID_PATTERN in constances.js), fall back to event capacity. On 400 response with campaign present, use campaign-full-error-msg or campaign-full-no-waitlist-error-msg keys and update submit button to waitlist or event-full state (disabled if no waitlist) to keep copy and UI consistent. This ensures campaign-level capacity gates take precedence over event-level gates when applicable.

nodes.summary: Date/time display logic: in-person events render in event timezone; webinars render in viewer timezone.
nodes.details: The date-time-helper.js utility implements a timezone selection rule: in-person events (those with a physical location) display their start/end times in the event's declared timezone, while webinars (virtual events) display times in the viewer's local timezone. This is enforced at render time, not at data fetch. Check event-libs/v1/utils/date-time-helper.js and event-agenda.js for the conditional logic that branches on event type.

nodes.summary: Do not override aria-label attributes on links decorated by Milo; only add new-tab behavior and security attributes (rel, target).
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/profile-cards/profile-cards.js, the static variant was manipulating link aria-labels that Milo had already populated during link decoration. The fix removes this override and restricts the block to only adding new-tab behavior (target, rel attributes) and standard security practices. This preserves accessibility semantics and prevents conflicts with upstream decoration logic. When extending Milo-decorated elements, add only orthogonal concerns (behavior, security) and avoid re-setting semantic attributes.

nodes.summary: Country field defaulting follows a strict priority order: consentStringId > IMS profile countryCode > cookie > navigator.language (only when locale has region).
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js, the country select prefill must respect this hierarchy: (1) never overwrite an existing attendee's consentStringId; (2) use IMS profile countryCode as primary default when signed in; (3) fall back to international_cookie; (4) use navigator.language only if the locale includes a region code (e.g. 'en-US', not 'en'). Use the synchronous findOptionByCountryCode helper to locate matching options. This prevents leaving the field empty and ensures attendee consent data is never lost during form personalization.

nodes.summary: Auto blocks in event-libs decorate.js support multiple links per block identifier; use Object.entries iteration to process all matching links.
nodes.details: The processAutoBlockLinks function in event-libs/v1/utils/decorate.js was refactored to iterate over block identifiers using Object.entries and process all matching links for each auto block, not just the first. This enables chrono-box and similar auto blocks to reference multiple schedule links in a single document. Future modifications to link replacement logic should preserve this multi-link support pattern.

nodes.summary: Do not assume rsvpData arrival timing relative to async attendee personalization; subscribe before async work and re-check after await to avoid race conditions in RSVP state transitions.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js, rsvpData subscriptions must be established before initiating async personalization flows (e.g., attendee profile fetches). After awaiting async work, re-check the RSVP status to ensure registered/waitlisted state is captured even if the status update arrived during the async operation. This pattern prevents users from landing on incorrect form states when RSVP confirmations race with personalization. The profile.js preload fallback writes should also be hardened to ensure consistent state. See test/unit/blocks/events-form/events-form.test.js and test/unit/scripts/profile.test.js for regression test patterns.

nodes.summary: Consent suite visibility and country-region capture follow a locale-aware, metadata-driven pattern: force-consent-collection metadata controls suite visibility; country picker data-country-code maps to payload.countryRegion; consent index URL uses locale-prefixed fallback pattern matching promotional-content.
nodes.details: In events-form.js, the consent suite (country picker + terms) is conditionally rendered based on user type (guest) OR force-consent-collection metadata being true. Country pre-selection logic runs whenever the suite is present. The consent query index JSON is fetched via getConsentQueryIndexUrl() using getLocale() + FALLBACK_LOCALES pattern (same as promotional-content), not a static URL. On form submit, the selected country option's data-country-code attribute is extracted and sent as payload.countryRegion in the baseAttendee object; BASE_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER already whitelists this field. This establishes the contract: force-consent-collection is a boolean metadata flag that overrides guest-only consent visibility, and country selection always populates countryRegion when the suite is shown.

nodes.summary: Campaign-aware RSVP registration: when campaignId URL param is present, fetch campaign capacity and apply waitlist rules before attendee creation.
nodes.details: In esp-controller.js, the getAndCreateAndAddAttendee flow checks for campaignId in the attendee payload. If present and event is not full, call getCampaign(eventId, campaignId) to fetch campaign capacity (attendeeLimit, attendeeCount, waitlistAttendeeCount). Apply waitlist logic: if attendeeLimit === attendeeCount, mark waitlisted; if attendeeLimit > attendeeCount and waitlistAttendeeCount > 0, mark waitlisted; if attendeeLimit > attendeeCount and waitlistAttendeeCount === 0, register normally. If no attendeeLimit, pass campaignId without campaign logic. Skip campaign lookup when event is already full. campaignId is sanitized in events-form.js (regex ^[\w-]{1,128}$) and added to EVENT_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER in data-utils.js so it flows into the event attendee API body.

nodes.summary: ESP environment detection uses URL query params with fallback chain: ?espenv or ?eccEnv → metadata event-service-env → prod default.
nodes.details: In esp-controller.js and event-subscription-form.js, environment resolution follows: check URL params (?espenv=<env> or ?eccEnv=<env>) first, then fall back to metadata('event-service-env'), then default to prod. When resolving CONFIG.ENDPOINTS in event-subscription-form.js, use getEventServiceEnv().name. This replaces hostname/domain sniffing and enables explicit per-request env override. Add 404-specific Lana logging in esp-controller.js when an event is not found in the selected ESP env.

nodes.summary: Do not rely on hashchange events to open modals when the target hash is already present in the URL; force a re-trigger by clearing and re-setting the hash.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/chrono-box/chrono-box.js, clicking an RSVP link when the URL hash already matches the modal target will not fire a hashchange event, preventing Milo's modal listener from triggering. The fix: clear the hash, then re-set it to the target value to force the event. Guard against double-triggering by checking if the modal is already rendered before re-setting the hash. This pattern applies to any Milo modal integration where the same hash may be clicked multiple times in a session.

nodes.summary: Do not rely on bubble-phase listeners to fire before page unload triggered by a same-target handler; use capture phase for tracking that must survive redirect.
nodes.details: In event-libs/scripts/meta-pixel.js, the attachLeadTracking() function attaches a click listener to document. If a button handler on the same target calls preventDefault() and triggers a redirect (e.g., via signIn()), the page unloads before the bubble-phase listener fires. Solution: pass { capture: true } as the third argument to addEventListener() so the tracking fires during the capture phase (document → target), before the button's bubble-phase handler runs. This pattern applies to any analytics/tracking that must complete before a same-target handler causes navigation.

nodes.summary: Page-schedule-indexer operates as a non-prod-only background service; loads conditionally on chrono-box presence and environment, indexes via ESP API without UI.
nodes.details: The page-schedule-indexer (event-libs/v1/features/indexer-widget/) is a background indexing service that auto-discovers and indexes unindexed schedules in non-prod environments only. Load is gated by two conditions in libs.js: (1) presence of DOM elements with data-schedule-id attribute, and (2) environment check via getEventConfig().miloConfig.env.name !== 'prod'. The indexer calls ESP API endpoints to index schedules and returns early if all schedules are already indexed or unindexable. Meta-pixel loading is also conditional on metadata presence. This pattern establishes that indexing is a non-user-facing, environment-aware background task, not a visible widget.

nodes.summary: HTML5 pattern and title attributes on text inputs enable regex-based client-side validation with custom browser tooltips; configure via Pattern and Title columns in form data JSON.
nodes.details: The events-form block's createInput function now accepts pattern and title attributes from the form data config JSON (normalized by lowercaseKeys utility). Authors add Pattern and Title columns to their config to enforce format validation—e.g., a URL field with Pattern: 'https?://.*' and Title: 'Please enter a valid URL' will trigger browser-native validation on submit and display the custom message in the validation tooltip. This pattern applies to any text input field in the events-form block.

nodes.summary: Carousel late-loading uses `is-delayed` class with `requestAnimationFrame` to prevent layout shift on initial render; consumers must apply this class and let carousel remove it after first paint.
nodes.details: The `milo-carousel` component implements a late-loading pattern via `is-delayed` CSS class and `requestAnimationFrame` in milo-carousel.js to defer carousel initialization until after the first browser paint, preventing layout thrashing. Consumers (profile-cards, bento-cards) must apply `is-delayed` to the carousel container; the component removes it once mounted. This pattern is critical for avoiding Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) on pages with multiple carousels. The CSS hides carousel controls while `is-delayed` is present, and JS removes the class after rAF callback completes.

nodes.summary: Meta Pixel tracking in event-libs uses a dual-mode metadata gate (martech vs. pixel-id) with safe fbq wrapper and BlockMediator subscription guard to prevent false positives on hydration.
nodes.details: The meta-pixel script (event-libs/scripts/meta-pixel.js) supports two modes via the `meta-pixel` metadata tag: (1) martech mode — Adobe Launch manages the pixel, only RSVP triggers attach; (2) pixel-id mode — in-page bootstrap with the given ID. All fbq calls wrap in safeFbq (try/catch + existence check) to prevent page breakage. CompleteRegistration event guards against false positives on initial hydration by subscribing to BlockMediator's rsvpData and checking registration state, not firing on page-load hydration. The script loads via eventsDelayedActions() dynamic import to avoid LCP impact. ViewContent fires once per page via IntersectionObserver on RSVP button scroll; Lead fires on every click via document-level delegation.

nodes.summary: Blocks that depend on hydrated DOM must await the hydration promise before init; hydration is triggered synchronously but resolved asynchronously by blocks that need it.
nodes.details: decorateEvent() in event-libs/v1/utils/decorate.js calls setHydrationPromise(hydrateBlocks(parent)) without awaiting, keeping decorateEvent synchronous. Blocks requiring hydrated DOM (identified by .hydrate class) must dynamically import the hydrate module and await getHydrationPromise() before their init logic runs. This pattern is implemented in event-libs/v1/blocks/image-links/image-links.js: check classList.contains('hydrate'), then await the promise from getHydrationPromise(). Non-hydrate blocks skip the import entirely, avoiding unnecessary module load.

nodes.summary: Chrono-box block exposes parsed schedule JSON on DOM via `data-tf-schedule-json` attribute for extension and third-party consumer access.
nodes.details: After the chrono-box block (event-libs/v1/blocks/chrono-box/chrono-box.js) resolves the schedule, store the parsed schedule object as `JSON.stringify(thisSchedule)` in the `data-tf-schedule-json` attribute on the block root element. This must occur after schedule resolution but before inner HTML is cleared, ensuring the attribute persists for the element's lifetime. Extensions and other DOM consumers can retrieve and parse this via `document.querySelector('.chrono-box')?.getAttribute('data-tf-schedule-json')` followed by `JSON.parse()`. This pattern enables decoupled access to schedule data without requiring direct block API exposure.

nodes.summary: Timing framework exposes serverTime and avoidStreamEndFlag parameters to control event stream lifecycle and server-clock synchronization in chrono-box.
nodes.details: The timing-framework (worker.js, worker-traditional.js) now accepts serverTime and avoidStreamEndFlag parameters that propagate to chrono-box.js. serverTime synchronizes client-side event scheduling with server clock; avoidStreamEndFlag prevents premature stream termination. These parameters are documented in timing-framework/README.md and tested in testing.js. Future integrations with event-libs timing should pass these through the worker initialization to maintain clock alignment and stream stability.

nodes.summary: Hydrator pattern: read event metadata from HTML meta tags and transform into block-ready HTML structure during page initialization.
nodes.details: The hydrator logic in event-libs/v1/hydrate/hydrate.js and event-libs/v1/hydrate/image-links.js reads structured data from <meta> tags (e.g., event title, date, speaker info) and generates the DOM structure required by the image-links block before the block's decorate() function runs. This decouples content authoring (meta tags in page head) from block rendering (image-links.js), allowing authors to define event data once and have it hydrated into multiple block types. The pattern applies to any block that needs pre-computed or externally-sourced data at page load time.

nodes.summary: Do not render mailto links when host-email metadata is missing in DA cmsType projects; remove them during decoration.
